<!--
The corpus has admission rules, and they are stricter than copyright law
requires. CONTRIBUTING.md § "The rules that actually bite" has the reasoning.
An issue first is the right order — a text can pass all four and still be a
poor fit, and it's better to find that out before the work.
-->

**The work** <!-- title, author, date -->

**The edition** <!-- the specific printing or transcription: publisher, year, host, URL -->

**The four rules**

- [ ] The work is public domain by age
- [ ] The specific printing is pre-1929, or dedicated CC0 / marked public domain, or a faithful transcription of one
- [ ] I can name that edition exactly
- [ ] Any modern editorial layer (introductions, notes, modern punctuation) is absent, excluded, or marked

**Why it belongs here** <!-- what it adds that the Library doesn't have yet -->
